### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/knowledge-turso`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeTursoPlugin (symbol, a top-level class), turso_auth_token (literal, a string literal in knowledgeTursoSettingsSpecifiers; a string literal in specifiers), turso_url (literal, a string literal in knowledgeTursoSettingsSpecifiers; a string literal in specifiers))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via loadTranslations (symbol, a method of interface TranslationSink))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeTursoPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ddc96d8a4280c69305dd541005cacfbe3e58f4c5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `725450d7332a93ebd986957e5b38cf2111e4f768` — the merge of head `5c9170a0d8f717030b7f0661e1b00a2cafbe2b7d` into base `ddc96d8a4280c69305dd541005cacfbe3e58f4c5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 725450d7332a93ebd986957e5b38cf2111e4f768 && git checkout 725450d7332a93ebd986957e5b38cf2111e4f768
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ddc96d8a4280c69305dd541005cacfbe3e58f4c5 5c9170a0d8f717030b7f0661e1b00a2cafbe2b7d && git checkout -B drift-repro ddc96d8a4280c69305dd541005cacfbe3e58f4c5 && git merge --no-ff 5c9170a0d8f717030b7f0661e1b00a2cafbe2b7d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ddc96d8a4280c69305dd541005cacfbe3e58f4c5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ddc96d8a4280c69305dd541005cacfbe3e58f4c5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5c9170a0d8f717030b7f0661e1b00a2cafbe2b7d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/settings-contribution.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/plugin.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/__tests__/settings-contribution.test.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/package.json, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/vitest.config.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/knowledge.manifest.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/knowledge.manifest.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/knowledge-settings-retired-keys.pin.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/knowledge-settings-default-absent.pin.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/translations/{ar,de,en,es-ES,fr,ja-JP,ko,pt-BR,ru,zh-CN,zh-Hant}.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/__tests__/knowledge-settings-contribution.test.ts, pnpm-lock.yaml (the 3-line importer entry only) + read, not reviewed: packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts (registerManifest, getManifest, servedManifest, setMany), packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-settings-contribution.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service-plugin.ts, packages/core/src/capability-composition.ts (resolveKnowledgeStore), packages/verify/src/harness.required-providers.test.ts, packages/services/service-i18n/src/file-i18n-adapter.ts, packages/core/src/fallbacks/memory-i18n.ts, packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-source.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md; the two changesets and content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx are read for ② and for the DELIBERATE CORRECTION, as the landing rule requires.

Inputs read: card #37678 (body, 4 comments, the dev report 7215704211 included), card #37679 (body, 3 comments), PR #37902 (body, its comments, 26 files, net diff against the merge base b620c4b2c6; `origin/main` has not moved any of these paths since), and the 71 check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, the narrowing.** `PUT /api/settings/knowledge` naming `turso_url` or `turso_auth_token` is now `400 UNKNOWN_KEY` where the page does not carry the group, and `GET` no longer serves them there. RIGHT, and it is measured, not asserted: `setMany` refuses in its pre-flight loop (`if (!reg.scopes.has(key)) throw new UnknownKeyError`) before any write, the base manifest at head declares `chunk_target` alone, and both doors are pinned at the HTTP envelope in the no-store block of the new kernel test and in the retired-keys pin.
- **Where the page does not carry the group.** Three compositions, each correct against `resolveKnowledgeStore`: PostgreSQL (pgvector mounted, no Turso plugin); an in-memory platform database (the mount passes `url: ':memory:'`, so the plugin reads no setting); a host that hands the plugin its own `url` or `client`. In all three `opensFromSettings()` is false and nothing reads either key. The changeset names the first and the third; the second is the third seen from the capability mount.
- **Where it does.** `capability-composition.ts:351` passes `urlFromSettings: true` with no `url` for every other database, so `init()` reaches `contributeKnowledgeTursoSettings`. RIGHT: the group is back in front of the page, the PUT answers 200, `turso_auth_token` stays in `secretKeysOf('knowledge')`, and the boot-saved URL is opened by the store.
- **Mechanism (the card's fence: no new one).** RIGHT. It is `SettingsService.registerManifest`, which replaces the registry entry and carries `prev.actions` over (`const actions = prev?.actions ?? new Map()`), the same call `contributeKnowledgeSettings` makes for the `ai` embedder section. Ordering is declared, not incidental: knowledge-turso lists `com.objectstack.service.knowledge` in `optionalDependencies`, and that plugin lists `com.objectstack.service.settings`; the kernel test `use`s the store ahead of both on purpose and still gets the group. Nothing else in the repository registers the `knowledge` namespace, so no later registration drops it.
- **Manifest version 4 to 5.** RIGHT against the published spec: `settings-manifest.zod.ts:798` says "Increment when keys are renamed/removed".
- **Stored rows.** RIGHT: no code path deletes one; a saved `turso_url` is pinned as kept and unserved without the store, and as served with `source: global` and writable once a page declaring the group is registered again.
- **The 11 locale moves.** RIGHT. Read as text from the two trees: each bundle's removed hunk carries six string literals (group title, group description, two labels, two helps) and the matching block of `knowledgeTursoSettingsTranslations` carries the same six, in the same order, with `URL_EXAMPLES` expanded: 11 locales, 66 literals, 0 differences, and no added line in any bundle. They land at the same paths (`settings.knowledge.groups.turso`, `settings.knowledge.keys.*`). Both i18n implementations deep-merge in `loadTranslations`, so loading the group's subtree does not replace the rest of `settings.knowledge`, whichever `kernel:ready` handler runs first.
- **Specifiers.** RIGHT: the three specifiers moved verbatim, the cloud per-organization sentence included (#37680's fence held).
- **Public surface.** `@objectstack/knowledge-turso` gains five exports. Additive; judged under ② and N4.
- **#37679 N2.** RIGHT: the whole-body pin posts each of `adapter`, `over_fetch`, `enforce_rls` beside `chunk_target: 600`, asserts 400 and the stored 500, and carries its own control (the same `chunk_target` alone saves).
- **#37679 N4, the premise split.** The dev is RIGHT. On `main`, `knowledge-settings-contribution.test.ts:201` is the test-door post (`values: { adapter: 'turso', turso_url: ... }`) and is fixed. The card's second site is `SECRET_SOURCE.adapter: 'memory'` at :225-226, a `KnowledgeSource` literal handed to `KnowledgeServicePlugin`, never posted to the test door; `adapter` is `z.string()` with no `.optional()` in `knowledge-source.zod.ts:185`, so removing it would break the declaration. The one other test-door post that sent `adapter`, `knowledge-settings-default-absent.pin.test.ts:130`, is the right second site; it posts to an unregistered namespace and asserts `404 UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE`, so its body changes nothing it asserts. The card's acceptance ("the two test-door tests post only the Turso fields") is met.
- **Gate verdicts.** 61 success, 9 skipped, 1 failure. The failure is `Check Changeset`, judged below.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — confirmed on the tree: the diff touches no published schema and no governed path (`Governed Surface Queue Guard`: success); it narrows two doors of one settings namespace.

- **Level.** `.changeset/37678-knowledge-turso-settings-group.md` takes `patch` on `@objectstack/knowledge-turso` and `@objectstack/service-settings`. RIGHT under AGENTS.md: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". `@objectstack/service-knowledge` changes one test and publishes nothing: no entry owed.
- **Declared everywhere it must be.** The `!` is in the PR title and in the changeset's first line. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset, and say the same thing. The BREAKING paragraph is there. The ADR-0087 marker is exactly one, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, and the gate read it: the `Check Changeset` notice on the new file prints that exemption and its reason, and `check:adr-0087-registration` is inside a green lint job. The reason holds: a settings manifest is a runtime registration, nothing `objectstack migrate meta` reads names these keys.
- **Migration text.** Sufficient for both readers. A script author is told what is refused, that it is refused whole, and the one-line fix ("Drop the two keys from the body"). An operator who saved the keys is told the rows stay, are not served, change nothing, are read again once the store is mounted, and may be deleted but need not be. See N3 for one omission.
- **Check Changeset red, the DELIBERATE CORRECTION.** The gate's own message names two classes with opposite remedies. This is the second: `.changeset/37104-knowledge-settings-readers.md` is pending on the merge base, this PR changes what it describes, and the PR body declares the correction, names the note and quotes the three sentences. It is not a collision: the new note has its own issue-scoped name. The gate text and `landing-operations.md` both say this class stays red, is not restored from base, waits for no maintainer, and, for a diff that also changes code, is confirmed by the seat's same-head at-tier contract-review PASS judging each rewritten sentence. Judged here, sentence by sentence:
  1. Clause-② line. Before: "`PUT /api/settings/knowledge` refuses `adapter`, `over_fetch` and `enforce_rls` (`400 UNKNOWN_KEY`), where it stored them". After: "refuses a body naming `adapter`, `over_fetch` or `enforce_rls` (`400 UNKNOWN_KEY`) whole, where it stored them: no other key in that body is saved". TRUE CORRECTION: the pre-flight in `setMany` throws before any write, and the new N2 pin holds it. This is #37679 N2, the sentence triage called wrong.
  2. BREAKING paragraph. Before: "the write is now refused as an undeclared key." After: adds "and refused whole — no other key in that body is saved, so a body that also changes `chunk_target` saves nothing. Drop the retired key from the body." TRUE CORRECTION, same evidence, and it adds the fix the paragraph lacked.
  3. Turso bullet. Removed: "; the Turso group now says so and always shows, since the page no longer has an adapter select to gate it on". TRUE CORRECTION: this PR makes "always shows" false. What is left ("On PostgreSQL the store is pgvector, in the platform database, and neither is read.") stays true.
  No other sentence of that note is made false by this head: "manifest `version` 4" describes #37104's own step and the new note says "now `version` 5"; "Test connection checks the Turso fields only" still describes the handler.
  With this record at PASS the correction is confirmed; the gate stays red by design and no gate is changed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0], the "Test connection" button on a page without the Turso fields.** Answered: option B, a follow-up card after #37680, as the dev recommends. It is not a correctness problem on this head. The handler opens no connection and changes no state on any deployment; on a page without the group `values` carries neither key, so with an empty payload it answers `ok: true`, severity `info`, "No Turso URL configured — where the knowledge store is @objectstack/knowledge-turso (a platform database other than PostgreSQL) ... This checks the form only — no connection was attempted." Every clause of that is conditional and true on PostgreSQL, and it claims no connection. `main` has the same handler behind the same button on the same deployments; what changed is that the fields it speaks of are no longer beside it. That is a leftover control, user-visible and worth moving, not a wrong answer. Recorded as N1.
- **Deviation: surface grew past the claim.** Accepted, each piece needed. `settings-contribution.ts` is where the moved declaration and copy live; the alternative was 230 lines inside `plugin.ts`. The devDependency on `@objectstack/service-settings` is test-only: the source imports `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/spec/system` as types and reaches the settings and i18n services through `ctx.getService` with local structural interfaces, so the published package gains no runtime dependency. No cycle: service-settings depends on core, platform-objects, spec and types; service-knowledge depends on service-settings; neither names knowledge-turso (`Validate Package Dependencies`: success). The vitest alias is what `check:test-source-alias` demands for a workspace import in tests. The lockfile hunk is that one importer entry. `knowledge-settings-default-absent.pin.test.ts:130` is N4's real second site.
- **Deviation: the copy moved into knowledge-turso, not only out of service-settings.** Accepted, and the dev's reason is correct: service-settings' coverage test refuses copy for undeclared keys, and a devDependency from service-settings on knowledge-turso would close a cycle through service-knowledge.
- **Deviation: first WIP push ahead of overlap-check.** Noted; it has no bearing on this head. The later runs were clean and `origin/main` has not touched these paths.
- **Deviation: the three-package run is at 37106cf2ad.** Accepted: the two later commits change the two changesets, the docs line, a doc comment in `knowledge.manifest.ts`, two lines of the new test and the vitest alias, and `Test Core` (10 of 10 shards) is green on the head itself.
- **out_of_scope: the group description's "On PostgreSQL ... these fields are not read" is now never shown on PostgreSQL.** Correctly left for #37680, which the claim parks behind this card; moved verbatim per the fence.
- **Not measured locally (`check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`).** Covered: `Lint & Repo Gates` is success on the head.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5).** Nothing to find: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. The contribution is a registry write and an i18n load.
- No security finding raised, and none found: the group keeps `encrypted: true` and `type: 'password'`, both doors keep `manage_platform_settings`, and `resolveSettingsStoreUrl` is untouched.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real; it does not take a delivered capability away at the consumer. The capability is "the operator names the libSQL store in settings and the store opens it". Its one reader is `readStoreSettings` in knowledge-turso, under `urlFromSettings` with no `url` or `client`. On every composition where that reader runs, both doors answer as on `main` and the end-to-end pin (`harness.required-providers.test.ts`, the real capability mount, `settings.set('knowledge','turso_url', ...)` answering `saved`, then the store opening that file) is green on the head. On every composition where it does not run, the two keys were declared and read by nothing, which is what ADR-0049 forbids offering; an undeclared key answering `UNKNOWN_KEY` is the settings contract's standing answer (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts`), not a new refusal. So this is "implemented where delivered, retired where not", decided at the declaration by the one party that knows whether it reads the keys, and not a consumer-side narrowing of something the platform still promises.

Tried to break it:
- Init order with the store registered first: held by the declared `optionalDependencies` chain, pinned with the adverse `use` order.
- A later registration replacing the page without the group: no second registrant of `knowledge` exists in the tree.
- The re-registration dropping the page's actions: `registerManifest` carries them, pinned (`test` still answered after it, in both packages).
- The copy load clobbering the settings bundle's `settings.knowledge` subtree: both i18n implementations deep-merge.
- The contribution failing silently on a store-from-settings deployment, leaving a saved URL unread behind a default file: it needs a `knowledge` page that the knowledge service did not register or a host page using the id `turso` for something else; see N2. On the runtime's own mount it cannot happen, and the harness pin would go red if it did.
- A deployment that uses Turso with its own `url`: it never read the settings, so hiding them is the correct reading of the card's "mounted", which the card wrote more loosely than the reader's condition.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits (none affects correctness or the contract):

- N1 (nit) — "Test connection" stays on the base page and, without the store, checks fields the page no longer shows. Answer is true and inert (see ③). Follow-up card, option B: move the button and its `knowledgeTestActionHandler` registration into knowledge-turso's contribution, after #37680, which edits the same group.
- N2 (nit) — `init()` discards the boolean `contributeKnowledgeTursoSettings` returns. When it is false while the store still reads from settings (a host `knowledge` page that uses the id `turso` without declaring the keys, or a page registered after this `init()`), `readStoreSettings` maps `SETTINGS_UNKNOWN_KEY` to "nothing saved" and the store opens its default file with no log line saying the fields are not on the page. Not reachable through the runtime's mount. A warn on `false` under `opensFromSettings()` would close it; follow-up or accepted deviation.
- N3 (nit) — the new changeset's tidy sentence names the `knowledge` setting rows but not the `sys_secret` row a saved `turso_auth_token` points at. Without the store there is now no API door that clears that key, so direct deletion is the only way to retire the stored token, and `settings-service.ts` itself calls an orphaned `sys_secret` row "a decryptable copy of the credential". One clause on the prose face would complete it ("and the `sys_secret` row its handle names"). No production deployment holds such a row today.
- N4 (nit) — `withKnowledgeTursoSection` composes from the copy `getManifest` serves, where the mechanism it cites composes from the declaration and says why (`knowledge-settings-contribution.ts`: a served copy carries option-source tables in place of declared ones). No `knowledge` key has an option source, so `servedManifest` returns the registered object itself today and the two are identical. Also, of the five new exports, `KNOWLEDGE_SETTINGS_NAMESPACE` is a generic name on a store package's permanent surface. Accepted deviation.
